events.title: Alfred Nobel's will creates the Nobel Prizes
events.summary: The inventor of dynamite's will creates the prizes.
events.description: On November 27, 1895, the Nobel Prizes were established through the will of Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist, engineer, and industrialist who invented dynamite and other powerful explosives.
events.notificationTitle: The will behind the Nobel Prizes
events.notificationBody: In 1895, Alfred Nobel's will established the Nobel Prizes.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 27

events.title: The first Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
events.summary: A New York tradition begins; the giant balloons arrive three years later.
events.description: On November 27, 1924, the first Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was held in New York City. It became an American tradition, known especially for the huge balloons introduced in 1927.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 27

events.title: The Treaty of Neuilly sets peace terms for Bulgaria
events.summary: Bulgaria and the Allies sign a post-World War I settlement.
events.description: On November 27, 1919, the Treaty of Neuilly, setting out the post-World War I peace terms for Bulgaria, was signed between Bulgaria and the Allied powers.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 27

events.title: Anders Celsius is born
events.dateNote: Date as given by Britannica; Sweden then used its own transitional calendar.
events.summary: The Swedish astronomer is born.
events.description: On November 27, 1701, the Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 27

events.title: Albania declares independence
events.summary: Delegates at Vlore proclaim an independent Albania.
events.description: On November 28, 1912, Albanian national delegates led by Ismail Qemal issued the Vlore proclamation, declaring Albania's independence.
events.notificationBody: In 1912, Albania declared its independence at Vlore.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 28

events.title: Nancy Astor becomes the first woman to sit in the House of Commons
events.summary: A milestone for women in British politics.
events.description: On November 28, 1919, Lady Astor became the first woman to sit in the British House of Commons.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 28

events.title: Mauritania declares independence
events.summary: The West African country leaves the French Community.
events.description: On November 28, 1960, Mauritania declared its independence and left the French Community.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 28

events.title: The Tehran Conference opens
events.summary: Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin meet in Iran.
events.description: On November 28, 1943, the Tehran Conference opened, bringing together US President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin, who pressed for an invasion of France.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 28

events.title: Richard Byrd flies over the South Pole
events.summary: An American aviator crosses the bottom of the world by air.
events.description: On November 29, 1929, American pioneer aviator Richard E. Byrd flew over the South Pole.
events.notificationTitle: Flying over the bottom of the world
events.notificationBody: In 1929, Richard Byrd flew over the South Pole.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 29

events.title: Polish cadets launch the November Insurrection
events.summary: An uprising in Warsaw challenges Russian rule.
events.description: On November 29, 1830, a Polish secret society of infantry cadets staged an uprising in Warsaw, beginning the November Insurrection.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 29

events.title: Louisa May Alcott is born
events.summary: The author of Little Women is born in Pennsylvania.
events.description: On November 29, 1832, Louisa May Alcott, best known for her novel Little Women, was born in Pennsylvania.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 29

events.title: The UN votes to partition Palestine
events.summary: Resolution 181 proposes Arab and Jewish states and an international Jerusalem.
events.description: On November 29, 1947, the United Nations General Assembly passed Resolution 181, which called for the partition of Palestine into Arab and Jewish states and for placing Jerusalem under a special international regime.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 29

events.title: Barbados becomes independent
events.summary: The Caribbean island gains full independence from Britain.
events.description: On November 30, 1966, Barbados, which had gained internal self-rule in 1961, achieved full independence from Britain.
events.notificationBody: In 1966, Barbados achieved full independence from Britain.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 30

events.title: Britain and the US sign preliminary peace articles
events.summary: The first step toward ending the American Revolution is agreed in Paris.
events.description: On November 30, 1782, Britain and the United States signed the preliminary articles of the Treaty of Paris, part of the Peace of Paris that concluded the American Revolution.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 30

events.title: Michael Jackson releases Thriller
events.summary: It becomes the best-selling album in the world.
events.description: On November 30, 1982, Michael Jackson released Thriller, which became the best-selling album in the world and won a record eight Grammy Awards.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 30

events.title: The Stone of Scone returns to Scotland
events.summary: The coronation stone comes home 700 years after Edward I took it.
events.description: On November 30, 1996, the Stone of Scone, a block of gray sandstone, was returned to Scotland 700 years after King Edward I took it to England as war booty.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 30

events.title: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat
events.summary: Her arrest in Montgomery sparks a 381-day boycott.
events.description: On December 1, 1955, in Montgomery, Alabama, Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat to a white passenger in violation of segregation laws and was arrested, sparking a 381-day bus boycott led by Martin Luther King, Jr.
events.notificationBody: In 1955, Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat in Montgomery.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 1

events.title: Ford debuts the moving assembly line
events.summary: Model T production is transformed at Highland Park, Michigan.
events.description: On December 1, 1913, the world's first moving assembly line debuted at a Ford factory in Highland Park, Michigan, manufacturing Model Ts. Henry Ford's innovation revolutionized the auto industry.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 1

events.title: The first World AIDS Day is held
events.summary: A global day of awareness begins.
events.description: On December 1, 1988, the first World AIDS Day was held.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 1

events.title: The Pact of Locarno is signed
events.summary: Five European powers sign agreements meant to secure peace in western Europe.
events.description: On December 1, 1925, Germany, France, Belgium, Great Britain, and Italy signed the Pact of Locarno, a series of agreements intended to guarantee peace in western Europe.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 1

events.title: Scientists achieve the first controlled nuclear chain reaction
events.summary: Enrico Fermi's team makes history at the University of Chicago.
events.description: On December 2, 1942, scientists led by Enrico Fermi conducted the world's first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction at the University of Chicago.
events.notificationTitle: The day the atom was harnessed
events.notificationBody: In 1942, Enrico Fermi's team ran the first controlled nuclear chain reaction.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 2

events.title: The United Arab Emirates is formed
events.summary: Six emirates on the Arabian Peninsula unite.
events.description: On December 2, 1971, the United Arab Emirates was formed by the union of six small emirates on the Arabian Peninsula; a seventh joined in February 1972.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 2

events.title: Napoleon crowns himself emperor
events.summary: The ceremony in Paris takes place in the presence of the pope.
events.description: On December 2, 1804, Napoleon crowned himself emperor of France in the presence of Pope Pius VII.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 2

events.title: President Monroe sets out the Monroe Doctrine
events.summary: The US warns European powers away from the Western Hemisphere.
events.description: On December 2, 1823, in his annual message to Congress, President James Monroe declared that the United States would not interfere in European affairs and would treat any European attempt to control a nation in the Western Hemisphere as a hostile act. The policy became known as the Monroe Doctrine.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 2

events.title: Christiaan Barnard performs the first human heart transplant
events.summary: A Cape Town surgical team makes medical history.
events.description: On December 3, 1967, South African surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed the first human heart transplant, at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town.
events.notificationTitle: A new heart in Cape Town
events.notificationBody: In 1967, Christiaan Barnard performed the first human heart transplant.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 3

events.title: Gold miners fight at the Eureka Stockade
events.summary: Diggers in Victoria, Australia, clash with government forces.
events.description: On December 3, 1854, gold miners at the Eureka goldfield in Victoria, Australia, who had barricaded themselves inside a hastily built stockade, opened fire on the government forces surrounding them, the culmination of long-standing grievances.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 3

events.title: A Streetcar Named Desire opens on Broadway
events.summary: Tennessee Williams's play premieres with Marlon Brando.
events.description: On December 3, 1947, Tennessee Williams's A Streetcar Named Desire premiered on Broadway, starring Jessica Tandy, Kim Hunter, and Marlon Brando.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 3

events.title: Missionary Francis Xavier dies off the coast of China
events.summary: The leading Catholic missionary of his era dies of fever.
events.description: On December 3, 1552, St. Francis Xavier, the leading Roman Catholic missionary of modern times, died of fever off the coast of China.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 3
